options.filename: Pontocho paper lantern by James Disley in Kyoto.jpg
options.author: James Disley  from  Pontocho  street in Nakagyo, Kyoto
options.description: Pontochō centres around one long, narrow, cobbled alley running from Shijo-dōri to Sanjo-dōri, one block west of the Kamogawa in Kyoto.  Today the area, lit by traditional lanterns at night, contains a mix of very expensive restaurants - featuring outdoor riverside dining on wooden patios throughout the summer - geisha houses and tea houses, brothels, bars, and cheap eateries.  It has a unique atmosphere - elegance and traditional beauty really do balance with seediness and the slightest hint of danger. Pontochō / 先斗町

options.filename: US Navy 100203-N-4031K-050 Sailor participate in Japanese festival.jpg
options.author: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Steven Khor
options.description: ATSUGI, Japan (Feb. 3, 2010) Commanding Officer Capt. Eric Gardner, left, throws bags of soybeans to the people of Yamato at the city's Tenmangu shrine to celebrate Setsubun, or the day between two seasons. The bean throwing ceremony is conducted by a person considered to be the person of the year and passes on good luck and drives away evil spirits to anyone who catches the beans. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Steven Khor/Released)

options.filename: From Camp Zama to Ninomiya Shrine- Throwing Beans for Good Luck? (9507449).jpg
options.author: U.S. Army USAGJ by  Daisuke Sato
options.description:
Camp Zama community members recently stepped out to embrace Japanese tradition!
 About 50 participants, some of whom wore the mask of an “oni,” or devil, joined Army Community Service for a walking tour of Ninomiya Shrine near Sagamihara Housing Area. 
 
They eagerly took part in the traditional “Setsubun” bean-throwing ceremony, shouting, “Oni wa soto! Fuku wa uchi!” (“Evils out, good fortune in!”) while tossing roasted soybeans.

options.filename: Farmers of forty centuries - well furnished guest room in a Japanese inn.jpg
options.author: Unknown photographer Unknown photographer
options.description: Interior view of a well furnished guest room in a Japanese inn, where the meals are served on the matting floor and the bed is laid. The room is finished in natural unvarnished wood, with walls of sliding panels of translucent paper, which may open upon a porch, into a hallway or into another apartment; and with its bouquet, which may consist of a single large shapely branch of the purple leaved maple, having the cut end charred to preserve it fresh for a longer time, standing in water in the vase.
options.credit: F. H. King,  Farmers of forty centuries , 1911, p. 394 (bottom).
